$comment: The expo-updates fingerprints of the binaries currently in users' hands.
An `eas update` only reaches a build whose fingerprint matches exactly;
publishing to any other value reports success and reaches zero devices,
with no error anywhere. scripts/verify-ota-target.mjs compares the working
tree against this file and refuses to publish on a mismatch.
Update this file in the same commit that ships a new binary, and never to
silence the preflight — a mismatch means the update cannot land, not that

android.$note: Submitted to Play closed alpha 2026-09-04 (EAS build 692255d0, submission a54d7333, commit 611374d). Play production promotion pending; until it lands most Android users still run 65. First store binary built with ARM ABIs only (#104) and React Native compiled from source with the EAS CMake hook (#102).

ios.$note: Submitted to the TestFlight internal group 2026-09-04 (EAS build 122f1e51, commit a08933b). App Store review pending; until it lands most iOS users still run 47. NOT reachable by an OTA from main: eas.json is a fingerprint input and #104 changed it after this build, so a clean checkout of main fingerprints iOS to f78a828af94230d8a3758701f06c46a082d1e7f9.
